And when they were hard pressed, they fled to Baghdad
and urged the Sultan to go in person to confront the Ma'addites.
And when he set out from Baghdad,
news of him reached al-Basasiri,
and he plundered Mosul terribly,
and departed into the desert.
Then the Sultan, when he reached Mosul,
found it completely devastated.
And it was also told to him concerning Ibrahim Yanal, his brother on his mother's side,
that he was meditating rebellion,
and letters were coming to him from the Caliph of Egypt.
Therefore, because the Sultan feared lest he gain control over Persia and make the armies of the Ghuzz Turkmens rebel with him,
he hastily set out for Persia,
and entered and took up residence in Hamadan.
And he sent a force against his brother in the mountains of Shahrazur,
and captured him and killed him.
Now al-Basasiri and Quraysh, the commanders of the armies, when they heard that the Sultan had gone far away,
came to Baghdad and seized control of it easily.
And they seized the Caliph al-Qa'im, mounted him on a camel,
and sent him to Haditha,
and plundered the palace.
And they proclaimed al-Mustansir, the Caliph of Egypt, in Baghdad,
and they also struck dinars and dirhams in his name.
And they appointed judges, legal scholars, and reciters,
and dressed them in white instead of black, according to the custom of the Egyptians.
As for the vizier, Ra'is al-Ru'asa,
because he had brought the Ghuzz to Baghdad,
they put him inside the hide of a newly flayed ox,
and sewed it up over him,
and left his face uncovered,
with the horns of the ox above his head.
And they impaled him, having cast hooks into his throat,
and he remained being roasted the whole day.
And he died after having received spittle, insults, and even curses from the common people of Baghdad,
because on his account all these evils had happened.
Then the mother of the Caliph al-Qa'im sent word to al-Basasiri from where she was hiding, saying,
"Behold, I am dying of hunger,
and I beg that you have mercy on me."
Then he sent and brought her, and lodged her in one of the houses of the palace,
and assigned her two of her maidservants to serve her,
and apportioned to them twelve litras of bread every day,
and four litras of meat, by Baghdad weight.
Now this woman (handmaid) was an Armenian by race.
